actual: ESLint completed with 0 errors but 44 warnings; the guide requires zero warnings.
197 test files passed; 1,195 tests passed and 1 skipped. The skipped case is the live Supabase integration test, disabled because RUN_LIVE_SUPABASE_TESTS is unset.
Next.js production build completed successfully; only a stale Browserslist data warning was emitted.
Production dependency audit exits non-zero with high-severity browserslist and fast-uri findings; ajv appears as a transitive high-severity path in the JSON report.
Full dependency audit exits non-zero with 13 high-severity findings (17 total).
Deployed migration list and repository each contain 273 migrations; the latest head is 20260902135923 monthly_overhead_analytics_events.
Estimator save, rate update, and historical snapshot RPC paths were callable from the deployed app.
Run identity, production URL, deployed commit, migration head, ledger, and report are recorded.
Valid Lite owner login reached /owner/estimator and session persisted across refresh.
The generic incomplete-onboarding expectation is intentionally overridden for Lite/Base: the Lite owner is allowed into the costing workspace and is not sent through the full-suite onboarding route.
Archived/deferred owner routes followed the product boundary: operational paths redirected or showed a Base upgrade wall; public unknown tracking token showed a safe link-not-found notice.
Lite navigation contains only Cost Estimate, Yarn Rate Book, Saved Costings, Billing, and Settings; deferred operational modules are not active navigation promises.
Representative grey-fabric costing matched the manual yarn math and included the required positive loom rate.
Two warp layers plus one weft layer each contributed once; layer totals and combined subtotal were exact.
GST changed the affected yarn base cost with decimal-safe rounding; 5% on warp changed the representative production cost from 27.39/m to 27.68/m.
60 inches and 152.4 centimetres produced the same 27.39/m result and the UI showed the converted equivalent.
Paise-per-pick mode converted 2 paise/pick across 60 picks to a 1.20/m loom cost without a 100x unit error.
Outsourced sizing at 1.50/kg added the expected charge on 5.50kg warp consumption; switching in-house removed the direct charge and kept it within overhead treatment.
Winding, processing, and finishing inputs changed production cost only when enabled; commission/transport mismatch required acknowledgement before save.
Direct overhead preserved a distinct source and monthly mode reconciled 1,150,000 monthly costs over 90,000m to 12.78/m after capacity inputs were complete.
Capacity calculation showed 24 looms × 144.23m/day × 26 days = 89,999.52m and used the rated-capacity denominator.
Zero weaving rate blocked readiness with a field-specific message; no false cost result or save was allowed.
The calculation engine rejects commission plus target margin at or above 100% with an explicit invalid quote message; full browser mutation was not required for this code-path check.
Saved quality creation, Rate Book update, load/reprice, favourite, archive/restore, duplicate draft, search, sort, and compare flows were exercised. Deletion was not invoked.
Draft recovery and collision handling are covered by the estimator client and automated tests; no destructive crash simulation was performed in production.
Changing the current Rate Book value from 191 to 192 updated the saved recipe but left the v1 quote snapshot at 191 and production cost 34.31/m.
Saved-costing comparison economics were loaded from immutable snapshots, but the calculation-detail UI rendered a non-applicable multi-layer warp rate as 0/kg instead of Not available/Multiple.
The saved Lite quality has an immutable v1 costing history record with the complete snapshot, assumptions, and INR_HALF_UP_2 rounding policy.
English works, but Hindi and Gujarati switch successfully into heavily mixed, grammatically awkward copy with untranslated high-risk terms such as margin, defaults, and account data.
